title: Compact fingerprint + windowed LRU cache for embeddings service (prefix-aware duplicate suppression)
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: The embeddings endpoint is a major cost and latency contributor due to repeated identical or near-identical input sequences across tenants and routes. Current cache entries are large (full hashed payloads), eviction is naïve LRU, and prefix-related duplicates (same doc with different metadata or prefixes) cause waste and cache churn. Goal: introduce a compact fingerprint-based cache plus a windowed LRU architecture that is prefix-aware, reduces memfootprint, and provides predictable invalidation semantics across model/version changes.
background: Observed symptoms: 99th percentile latency spikes correlated with synchronous cache misses; 40% of embedding requests in one sample were exact duplicate inputs within a 30-minute window; cache memory pressure from storing full input blobs; stale entries after model retokenization or semantic indexing updates. Existing tickets (ENG-7283, ENG-8421) tackled specific pieces (dedupe/hash invalidation) but left opportunities for a consolidated lightweight fingerprint + window eviction model that scales to high QPS and multi-tenant namespaces.
proposal: 1) Use a 64-bit content fingerprint (xxh3_64 or farmhash64) computed over a normalized payload (prefix stripped by canonical rules) plus a 16-bit model-version tag to form a 80-bit compact key. 2) Implement a windowed LRU: in-memory segmented LRU windows (e.g., 5s micro-window buckets + 1h aging ring) to keep hot items cached while bounding worst-case eviction overhead. 3) Maintain prefix-index quotas: assign soft budget per prefix/route to avoid noisy neighbors. 4) Add a lightweight Bloom prefilter to quickly answer ‘definitely not cached’ for very hot negative paths and avoid DB/check overheads. 5) Introduce model-aware invalidation: every model or tokenizer change increments a version token; cached fingerprint entries include that token for fast global invalidation. 6) Expose metrics (fingerprint hit ratio, false positive rate for Bloom, per-prefix eviction counters, mem usage) and a /cache/admin endpoint for manual prune and diagnostics.

acceptance_criteria:
- End-to-end embedding request path uses compact fingerprint store for lookups for >=90% of eligible requests.
- Fingerprint cache reduces peak memory footprint relative to baseline by >=30% in standard workload.
- End-to-end median latency for embeddings improves or is unchanged; 95th/99th latency reduces by >=10% on workloads with duplicate contention.
- False positives from Bloom filter are <1% and do not cause correctness regressions.
- Can invalidate all cached entries for a model/version within 2s of version bump.
- Telemetry dashboards in Console showing fingerprint hit ratio, per-prefix eviction rates, and memory usage live for 7 days in canary.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for fingerprint normalization and determinism across language variants.
- Property tests verifying canonicalization (prefix-stripping rules).
- Integration test that simulates interleaved duplicates and verifies hits vs misses.
- Load test: replay 1M requests with realistic duplicate distribution, measure mem usage and tail latency.
- Chaos tests: inject spurious model-version bumps and validate global invalidation success and fallbacks.
- Regression: ensure embedding vector outputs are unchanged (bit-exact where expected) when cache hits vs cold compute.
risks:
- Hash collision risk with 64-bit fingerprint (mitigation: include model-version tag and a small validation step for very rarely flagged collisions).
- Bloom false positives causing unnecessary compute: tuned by target false positive rate and monitored metrics.
- Prefix budgets could deny cache to productive prefixes if configured too strictly (mitigation: dynamic rebalancing & throttling).
- Operational complexity: new admin APIs and observability must be in place before canary.
- Multi-tenant isolation bugs: ensure namespace separation and RBAC on /cache/admin endpoints.
